theory.intro: A unit fraction has a numerator of $1$. You can decide whether it is smaller or larger than $\tfrac{1}{2}$ by looking at its denominator.
facts: $\tfrac{1}{2}$ splits one whole into **two** equal parts.
For the same whole, a denominator greater than $2$ means more equal parts. Each part is smaller than a half.
steps: Look at the denominator of the unit fraction.
If the denominator is more than $2$, the fraction is **less** than $\tfrac{1}{2}$.
Compare to $\tfrac{1}{2}$: $\tfrac{1}{2}$ is the largest unit fraction except $1$ itself.

workedExamples.question_text:
Compare using $<$, $>$ or $=$.
a) $\frac{1}{5}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$
b) $\frac{1}{2}$ and one half
workedExamples.solution_text:
a) Splitting the same whole into $5$ equal parts gives smaller parts than splitting it into $2$ equal parts.
$\frac{1}{5}<\frac{1}{2}$
b) $\frac{1}{2}$ is one of two equal parts, so it is one half.
$\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$

workedExamples.question_text: Which of $\frac{1}{4}$, $\frac{1}{6}$ and $\frac{1}{10}$ is closest to $\frac{1}{2}$? Explain your answer without using decimals.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The smaller denominator gives the larger unit fraction.
$\frac{1}{10}<\frac{1}{6}<\frac{1}{4}<\frac{1}{2}$
All three are below a half. $\frac{1}{4}$ is the largest, so it is closest to a half.

foundation.solution_text:
$4>2$, so quarters are smaller than halves.
$\frac{1}{4}<\frac{1}{2}$

foundation.question_text: Is $\frac{1}{3}$ less than or greater than $\frac{1}{2}$?
foundation.solution_text:
A whole split into $3$ parts has smaller parts than a whole split into $2$ parts.
$\frac{1}{3}<\frac{1}{2}$

foundation.question_text: Which is closer to one whole: $\frac{1}{2}$ or $\frac{1}{5}$?
True or false: $\frac{1}{8}$ is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$ because $8>2$.
foundation.solution_text:
A larger denominator makes each unit part smaller.
The statement is **false**.

development.question_text:
A unit fraction is less than $\frac{1}{2}$ and has a denominator between $5$ and $7$.
What is it?
Which unit fractions with denominators from $2$ to $8$ are at least $\frac{1}{2}$?
development.solution_text:
Only denominator $2$ gives equality; all larger denominators give smaller parts.
$\frac{1}{2}$

Sixths are smaller parts than halves.
$\frac{1}{6}<\frac{1}{2}$

development.question_text:
One piece is $\frac{1}{3}$ of a strip.
Is it more or less than half the strip? Explain your answer.
development.solution_text:
The same strip split into $3$ equal parts has smaller parts than when it is split into $2$ equal parts.
$\frac{1}{3}<\frac{1}{2}$
The piece is less than half the strip.

development.question_text:
A unit fraction is greater than $\frac{1}{5}$ but less than $\frac{1}{2}$.
Give two possibilities.
development.solution_text:
The denominators can be $3$ and $4$.
$\frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{1}{4}$

mastery.question_text: Which unit fractions with denominators $2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10$ are less than or equal to $\frac{1}{2}$?
mastery.solution_text:
A denominator of $2$ gives one half. Each of the other denominators gives more, smaller equal parts of the same whole.
$\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{5},\frac{1}{6},\frac{1}{7},\frac{1}{8},\frac{1}{9},\frac{1}{10}$

mastery.question_text:
A student says there is a unit fraction strictly between $\frac{1}{2}$ and $1$.
Explain why this is impossible.
mastery.solution_text:
A unit fraction has numerator $1$.
$\frac{1}{2}$ is the largest proper unit fraction, so none lies between $\frac{1}{2}$ and $1$.

mastery.question_text: Without converting to decimals, compare $\frac{1}{10}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$.
mastery.solution_text:
The same whole split into $10$ equal parts has smaller parts than when it is split into $2$ equal parts.
$\frac{1}{10}<\frac{1}{2}$
